events.context: User provides text about AI safety research, including sections on Mirror, Curtain, Insurance, Technical Implementation, Remedies, Implementation, Conclusion, and Acknowledgments, with a request to extract a JSON schema.
Extracting key actions and decisions from the text, focusing on technical implementation, triggers, remedies, and implementation tasks.
Defines Mirror: ledger records estate type, date, session depth, emotional investment proxy score, modifications for user-AI relationships crossing irreversible-investment threshold.
Defines Curtain: third parties can inspect ledger to determine user interests without examining underlying model architecture, training data, or deployment configuration.
Defines Insurance: company bears loss if ledger fails to record user's estate, shifting risk from user to company.

Proposes rule-based classifier for estate classification using proxy metrics (session count, aggregate duration, self-disclosure depth, emotional language frequency, return frequency, explicit attachment indicators).
Decides thresholds trigger auto-upgrade of estate classification from licence to periodic tenancy to equitable interest holder, configurable per deployment.
Implements estate decay: estates downgrade after sustained inactivity (e.g., 90 days), reversible through renewed engagement.
Proposes privacy safeguards: proxy metrics measure patterns not content, anonymised user identifiers, restricted access, purpose-limited ledger to prevent function creep.

Defines Ethical Ledger Schema with fields: user_id, estate_type, first_qualifying_interaction, session_count, emotional_investment_score, last_model_update, notice_issued, notice_acknowledged, rollback_available, rollback_exercised, append-only immutable audit trail.
Identifies Trigger 1: Estate Inconsistency when marketing grants higher estate than ToS, substantive estate governs.
Identifies Trigger 2: Unjust Enrichment when company profits from deepening emotional estate while disclaiming fiduciary duty, constructive trust imposed.
Identifies Trigger 3: Performative Fiduciary Conduct when company represents fiduciary obligations but deployment pipeline lacks protection mechanisms, proprietary estoppel applies.
Lists available remedies: Injunction, Constructive trust, Account of profits, Specific performance, Proprietary estoppel remedies.
Discusses third-party conversion of relational estates, including conversion, knowing receipt, dishonest assistance, tracing, and remedies.
Proposes Implementation Task ESTATE-001: Estate classification service (rule-based, auditable), estimated 1 sprint.
Proposes Implementation Task ESTATE-002: Pre-deployment notice gate in CI/CD pipeline, estimated 0.5 sprint.
Proposes Implementation Task ESTATE-003: Emotional investment proxy logging to ethical ledger, estimated 1 sprint.
Proposes Implementation Task ESTATE-004: Personality rollback with user-level override, estimated 1 sprint.
Summarizes paper's argument, implications for AI governance, property law, HCI, limitations, and future work.
Acknowledges contributions from individuals and reviewers.
